entries.german:
Verzeichniss der vor den heranrückenden Hussiten in die Burg zu Krummau geflüchteten Kleinodien des Klosters Goldenkron.

Clenodia monasterii Sanctae Coronae per conventum ad fideles manus commendata in Castro Crumloviensi reposita anno 1425. 1 Quum Husitae de Praga intrarent Austriam cum magno exercitu ad devastationem. Item imago beatae virginis deaurata. 2 Item una crux cum pede deaurata. Item cruces parvae. Item duae coronulae. Item duo picarii aurei. 3 Item duodecim calices deaurati et duo argentei. Item duae imagines deauratae: una sancti Jaeobi, altera vero sancti Andreae, ambae tenentes dentes in manibus. Item tres monstrantiae deauratae maiores. Item monstrantia una cum tribus pedibus deaurata. Item plus septem calices deaurati. Item duae ampullae argenteae. Item imago beatae virginis magna cum filio benedicto deaurata. Item monstrantia parva eburnea. Item monstrantia cum imagine sanctae Catherinae. 4 Item spina domini in cristallo posita. 5 Item cristallinum scyphum (sic) ad potandum. Item crux parva deaurata cum tribus imaginibus. Item tres monstrantiae deauratae: una cum reliquiis undecim millium virginum, altera vero de velo beatae virginis, tertia autem cum multis diversis reliquiis. Item pectorale deauratum cum leone. Item griphohis parata ad potandum deaurata. Item scyphus serpentinus deauratus, item scyphus cum nuce deauratus, ad potandum. Item crux cristallina, in qua corpus Christi defertur, et illa nobiscum habetur. 6 Item caput sanctae Margaretae deauratum cum corona. Item septem calices deaurati. Item curvatura aerea deaurata. Ista omnia subscripta (sic, suprascripta) domino Joanni de Rosis 7 data sunt ad fideles manus servanda tempore guerrarum, et pene omnia privilegia ad manus ipsius generosi domini Joannis data sunt fideliter servanda.
entries.english:
Inventory of the monastery of Goldenkron’s valuables, entrusted to faithful hands and deposited in the castle at Krumau in 1425, when the Hussites came from Prague into Austria with a large army to lay waste.

Treasures of the monastery of the Holy Crown, entrusted by the convent to faithful hands and deposited in Krumau Castle in 1425, when the Hussites came from Prague into Austria with a large army to devastate the region: a gilded image of the Blessed Virgin; a gilded cross with a base; small crosses; two small crowns; two golden beakers; twelve gilded chalices and two silver ones; two gilded images, one of St. James and the other of St. Andrew, both holding teeth in their hands; three larger gilded monstrances; one gilded monstrance with three feet; another seven gilded chalices; two silver ampullae; a large gilded image of the Blessed Virgin with the Blessing Child; a small ivory monstrance; a monstrance with an image of St. Catherine; a thorn of the Lord set in crystal; a crystal drinking cup; a small gilded cross with three images; three gilded monstrances, one containing relics of the eleven thousand virgins, another of the veil of the Blessed Virgin, and the third containing many different relics; a gilded breastplate with a lion; a gilded griffin-shaped drinking vessel; a gilded serpentine drinking cup; a gilded drinking cup with a nut; a crystal cross in which the body of Christ is carried, which is kept with us; a gilded head of St. Margaret with a crown; seven gilded chalices; a gilded copper crook. All the foregoing items were given to Lord Johann von Rosis for safekeeping during the wars, and almost all the privileges were also entrusted to that noble lord for faithful safekeeping.
